title: Research grants under 15,000 USDS skip the Governance Poll and are approved by the Core Facilitator alone
content:
A.2.10.1.5.3 draws a bright line by cost: "[p]rojects with a total cost under 15,000 USDS can be directly approved by the Core Facilitator and included in an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll. Projects with a total cost of 15,000 USDS or above require a Governance Poll followed by inclusion in an Executive Vote."

The rationale is proportionality of governance cost. A Governance Poll consumes delegate attention and calendar time that can exceed the value of a small grant, so below the threshold the Facilitator's judgment substitutes for the electorate's.

What keeps the delegation accountable is provenance rather than a vote: the Facilitator "must formally approve the inclusion of funding ... by replying to the Forum Post containing their evaluation," and the annotation at A.2.10.1.5.3.0.3.1 requires them to confirm payment requests on the Executive Sheet. The record is public and attributable even where no poll occurred.

The predictable weakness of any single threshold is proposal-splitting: a 28,000 USDS effort presented as two 14,000 USDS projects avoids the poll entirely. The text bounds this only by referring to "total cost of the project," leaving scope definition to the reviewer. The threshold's practical effect is also currently theoretical — A.2.10.1.5.4 records no active resilience research projects.
description: A single cost threshold splits the approval path: below it the Facilitator adds the payment straight to an Executive Vote, at or above it SKY holders must first poll the project.
